686 distinct NEP proposals produce 737 comparison pairs; 51 proposals match more than one historical year. The NEP cost counts each proposal once. These are screened allocations, not confirmed duplicate costs. Overlapping chainage and incomplete chainage require scope review.

Potential repeated line items: FY2027 NEP → FY2026 GAA, then FY2025 GAA

Multi-purpose buildings, roads, bridges, and flood-control projects. The name screen found 283 FY2027 NEP lines with a 90% or higher title match in the FY2026 enacted GAA, and 454 with a 90% or higher title match in the FY2025 enacted GAA. Bridge candidates require overlapping plus-form chainage. Road matches are excluded when both stated ranges are disjoint; missing chainage is flagged for review. Different package, phase, stage, lot or segment labels require scope review. They may identify legitimate separate work or changes in how the same work is described; overlapping chainage still signals shared extent. Explicit opposing directions are excluded. For all categories, verify location, scope, phase, and completion status before treating a row as the same project. Explicit opposing directions are excluded as location conflicts. Amounts are in pesos. Title similarity is a screening lead, not proof that two appropriations cover the same scope.

PH location DB supplies current 20th Congress names through qualified geographic context and the strict local-map screening rules. Uncertain locations stay blank. Names describe geographic coverage, not sponsorship.

Of the NEP repeat candidates, how many survived into HGAB?

The 737 headline is a NEP-level comparison with old enacted GAA. Tracing the same proposal codes into HGAB 3rd reading gives 634 clearly retained comparison pairs, representing 591 distinct proposals. Potential links remain separate.

A proposal matched to two historical years counts twice in the pair column but once in the proposal column. Clear retention means a selected, scope-compatible normalized-title link in our current parser, not a certified work-scope audit. A potential retained link is a provisional selected counterpart. Missing links do not establish that HGAB removed the project.

For retained proposals, investigate whether old appropriations and HGAB fund the same component. For unmatched proposals, check renaming, segmentation, parser fragments and original pages before claiming removal. Amount changes on retained lines are allocation adjustments, not automatically insertion or removal.

Methodology and exclusions

Compare distinct allocation occurrence IDs within each stage only. FAPs and untrusted NEP primary titles excluded. Same normalized official PAP and either qualified municipality/province or same implementing office required. At least three shared distinctive nonnumeric title tokens required. Same base title after trailing geographic metadata removal, or ≥0.94 SequenceMatcher similarity with qualified municipality/province AND identical distinctive token sets, produces a candidate. Changed route-endpoint or other distinctive scope tokens veto even when text similarity is high. Different explicit bridge numbers identify different structures and veto a pair, even on the same bypass road. Direction, qualified-location and tranche conflicts veto. Explicit disjoint ranges veto. Printed range endpoints are assumed to be ordered min/max. Mixed bare/plus ranges retain an unknown endpoint: a known maximum at or below another range’s known minimum excludes positive overlap, without resolving length. Other mixed ranges remain incomplete; possible overlap is not certified overlap. No amount-equality requirement. Missing chainage never proves scope overlap.

  • Matching allocation occurrences does not establish duplicate contracts, duplicate payment, fraud or authorship. Different engineering components and legitimate amendments can share titles.
  • Office-only agreement is weaker than site evidence. Unresolved locations are never inferred from similar names.
  • Pair counts are not project counts: three linked records produce three pairs. Distinct occurrence counts are shown separately; amounts are not summed as loss.
  • Exact official PAP blocking, trusted-title requirements and conservative location rules miss possible cross-program, paraphrased or unresolved duplicates. No flag is not clearance.
  • Tranche differences are excluded from this conservative queue, not certified as legitimate. Missing chainage requires source and engineering-scope review.
  • NEP baseline includes source records outside the API. Its documented source-title confidence limits remain applicable.
